t.advisor.tx483f0: Drag to compare. The legacy list showed every database field as a column. The redesign keeps the five things an advisor scans for and puts actions next to the list. Client data in the legacy screenshot is blurred.
t.advisor.txdb370: Measured in the screens, projected for the business
t.advisor.txae9b8: These counts come straight from the legacy and redesigned screens.

t.advisor.txdd0f5: Dialogs and tabs to start a batch2 + 31 modal, 3 fields
t.advisor.txf5969: Tabs before content on a household76
t.advisor.txa7594: About these numbers. I didn’t have access to post-launch analytics, so the figures below are reasoned projections, not measured results. Each states its basis, and the validation plan further down shows how they would be checked.
t.advisor.txfaab0: ~50%Less time on quarter-end batch reportingBasis: the flow halved from 14 to 7 steps, and the dual list replaced by single selects.
t.advisor.txbff26: 25–35%Fewer “where is my report?” ticketsAssumes most reporting tickets are about status, now shown in the row.
t.advisor.txf7018: <1 hrSelf-serve firm onboarding, down from daysAssumes branding changes previously went through engineering tickets.
t.advisor.tx857c4: Same dayReport template changes, down from weeksAssumes templates were previously managed in code.
t.advisor.tx8889a: ~30%Faster ramp-up for new advisorsOne frame, table and toolbar pattern across all modules.
t.advisor.txc83a8: 0Brand themes shipped below WCAG AA contrastTarget, if the built-in contrast check blocks saving.

t.advisor.tx5c62a: Wealth, goals, accounts and documents on one page.
t.advisor.tx2c4e2: Three fields instead of three tabs, with status in the row.
t.advisor.tx3d11d: Admins build pages, advisors stitch reports.
t.advisor.tx2b576: Brand, logo and dashboards in one guided setup.
t.advisor.tx7ba4b: Two flat grids became a single household view where an advisor sees wealth, goals, accounts and documents without leaving the page.
t.advisor.tx66a49: RequirementThe stakeholder wireframe. A useful start that repeated legacy problems: three equal member cards, a panel duplicating the header, and seven tabs before any content.
t.advisor.tx9df94: What I changed from the brief
t.advisor.tx18e18: Merged the member cards and household panel into one summary line: AUM, account count, external ID, advisor.
t.advisor.txe999d: Added goal chips (College, Retirement, School, New Home) that came out of the card sort.
t.advisor.tx2f03f: Grouped the accounts table by goal, so the household reads like a financial plan.
t.advisor.txfb2a0: Cut the tabs to six, ordered by how often each is used.
t.advisor.tx00461: Moved Generate Report next to the documents it creates.
t.advisor.txac041: AfterHousehold details. One header answers “who is this and how much do we manage?”. The table below answers “for what?”.
t.advisor.tx2ca83: Summary line, not cardsAUM, accounts, external ID and advisor in one scannable row.
t.advisor.tx4b122: Goal chips with counts“2 College, 1 Retirement” shows the shape of a household before any table is read.
t.advisor.txb9007: Underlined tabsA familiar pattern with one active state, reused on the account page.
t.advisor.tx5785e: Accounts grouped by goalCollapsible groups replace a flat list; names link to account details.
t.advisor.tx7e2c6: Previous and next householdAdvisors work through their book in sequence without going back to the list.
t.advisor.tx1590b: AfterAccount documents. Status in the row itself: 95% with a spinner while generating, a check when done, a red label on failure.
t.advisor.tx9ef23: AfterAccount groups. Creating a goal and filling it with accounts happen on the same table.
t.advisor.tx33586: Batch report generation and the documents centre
t.advisor.tx966ff: Quarter-end means producing reports for every client at once. The legacy flow worked, but only for people who already knew it.
t.advisor.txf358e: BeforeRun Reports. Three tabs, a package picker, and reports moved one at a time with arrow buttons.
t.advisor.tx42c3e: BeforeBatch status. One row per report page, not per client, and a green-on-dark-green heatmap legend.
t.advisor.tx201de: Redesign: Households, select, Generate Report, pick report, pick as-of date, run, download from Documents.
t.advisor.tx8adfe: AfterStart where the advisor already is. Generate Report is the primary action on the households list, and the selection is the batch scope.
t.advisor.tx7c665: AfterThree fields instead of three tabs. Selected households carry over as chips. Preview checks a sample before running hundreds.
t.advisor.tx1e067: AfterConfirmation with a way back. A long batch job no longer starts silently; the toast offers Undo for a few seconds.
t.advisor.tx34bd8: AfterDocuments centre. One place for every generated report across the firm.
t.advisor.txe479c: Filters shown as chipsThe active filter is visible and removable; Clear all resets the view.
t.advisor.tx95d3f: Save filterQuarter-end repeats, so a view built once can be reused.
t.advisor.tx99b18: Group by batchThe same list works as a flat log or grouped by run.
t.advisor.txbbcba: Filter count badgeShows active filters even when the drawer is closed.
t.advisor.txe068c: Status in the rowProgress, Completed and Error replace the separate heatmap page.
t.advisor.tx82816: Flat view with an error in red.
t.advisor.tx43276: Report templates used to be built by engineering. I designed a two-level builder: super admins design reusable pages, and advisors stitch those pages into the reports they send.
t.advisor.tx2909b: ResearchAnalogous patterns. Settings panels from other domains and a site builder’s “add section, pages” menu informed the split between building and assembling.
t.advisor.txeb2d8: Most competitors put layout, data binding and assembly in one editor. That suits a firm’s designer but overwhelms an advisor who only wants to add a commentary page. Splitting the jobs by role protected the brand without blocking advisors. It was the most important decision of the year.
t.advisor.tx610f9: AfterPage library. Page types come straight from the QPR teardown.
t.advisor.tx87d9e: AfterStart from a layout. Thumbnails by page type with a realistic preview.
t.advisor.tx9eea0: AfterPage Builder canvas. Three panels, as in the research, with fewer controls in each.
t.advisor.tx34479: Page railThumbnails show the layout; “Add another page” stays quiet.
t.advisor.txe0ee9: Locked header and footerCompliance content can’t be deleted by accident.
t.advisor.tx90714: Content tilesThe selected tile renders real chart output.
t.advisor.tx5ec32: Empty tiles prompt an action“Select Data Type” says exactly what’s needed next.
t.advisor.txc447b: Page and tile propertiesSettings follow the selection.
t.advisor.txfbbd8: Preview before SaveA separate, darker action, never confused with saving.
t.advisor.tx13a11: AfterReport Stitcher. Advisors order approved pages; Save a Copy branches a template safely.
t.advisor.tx4ea93: AfterGenerate. The same three-decision pattern as batch reports.
t.advisor.tx2d4c5: AfterRendered output. A page produced through the builder.
t.advisor.txa61b7: To sell to more firms, the platform had to take on each firm’s brand and defaults without engineering work. I turned a rough wireframe flow into a guided, four-tab setup.
t.advisor.txa150b: BeforeStarting point. A long create form, then redirects to separate view and edit pages.
t.advisor.tx65054: RequirementDefault dashboards. Super admins set household and account dashboards once for every advisor.
t.advisor.tx73995: AfterColour scheme with live preview. Intentionally showing a failing palette to demonstrate the guard rail.
t.advisor.txecb66: One page, four tabsGeneral, Colour, Logo and Dashboard replace create-then-redirect.
t.advisor.txf0c71: Colours named by where they appear“Title bar” and “Footer bar”, not hex codes.
t.advisor.tx304f3: Live report previewEvery change shows on a miniature report page.
t.advisor.tx54ac3: Built-in accessibility check“Accessibility Fail” flags low contrast before clients see it.
t.advisor.tx3bb87: Links into the builderPage Builder and Report Stitcher are one click away.
t.advisor.tx9adde: AfterFirms list, shared table pattern.
t.advisor.txb0e73: UX researcher and UX/UI designer, end to end
t.advisor.tx7277c: I ran the research and the heuristic audit, then designed the task flows, wireframes, high-fidelity UI and shared pattern library for all four modules.
t.advisor.txb533f: A powerful engine with an interface built for the people who maintain it
t.advisor.txe7252: The platform did a lot: trading, modelling, monitoring and reporting. But every screen exposed the data model directly. Advisors had to translate their question, “how is the Smith family doing?”, into filters on a 30-column account grid.
t.advisor.tx6e01c: 19+columns on the client list, mostly address fragments
t.advisor.tx9a225: 26fields in one edit modal, with placeholder dates of 01/01/1900
t.advisor.tx69c9c: ~30columns on the accounts grid, with no grouping
t.advisor.txe8970: 14steps to run a batch of reports and download them
t.advisor.tx820c3: BeforeAccounts grid. A heatmap sidebar, about 30 columns, and legal account titles as the only way to tell accounts apart. Data blurred.
t.advisor.tx10502: BeforeEdit client. 26 equal-weight fields with no grouping. Default dates such as 01/01/1900 show the data quality problem this creates.
t.advisor.txf13f6: Move from an operations console to an advisor-facing platform that can be white-labelled and sold to more advisory firms.
t.advisor.tx9ef0b: See a household at a glance, produce polished reports for many clients at once, and trust that those reports went out.
t.advisor.tx3c1da: The data model and reporting engine stayed the same. Every design had to map onto existing clients, accounts, batches and templates.
t.advisor.tx76314: Understanding the work before redrawing the screens
t.advisor.tx9c0fc: Expert users and limited access to them called for mixed methods.
t.advisor.tx218d3: Requirement analysisBroke product tickets into step-by-step task flows. The batch-report ticket became the 8-step workflow behind Module 2.
t.advisor.txea9e3: Competitor demo studyCaptured the first 11 minutes of a Black Diamond demo frame by frame to map templates, page building and the report queue.
t.advisor.tx86594: Competitive and analogous auditLooked beyond wealth tech: print management, project tools and drag-and-drop site builders.
t.advisor.tx629b9: Card sortingA sticky-note sort of the account and household tabs set their order and naming.
t.advisor.tx9aec2: Artifact analysisTook apart the 18-page Quarterly Performance Review to list the page types a builder would need.
t.advisor.tx69606: Heuristic evaluationScored legacy screens against Nielsen’s 10 heuristics with severity, so fixes were ranked by impact.
t.advisor.txa027c: ResearchCompetitor demo, frame by frame. Black Diamond’s template editor: page thumbnails on the left, the canvas in the centre, properties on the right. I adopted this three-panel layout and simplified it.
t.advisor.tx4780e: RequirementThe product ticket. Start from a list, filter, select, generate, watch progress, zip, and file each report in the right household.
t.advisor.tx22bc2: ArtifactThe Quarterly Performance Review. Taking the output apart page by page gave the builder its vocabulary: page types, header and footer zones, chart and table tiles.
t.advisor.txf5d35: AdvisorManages a book of households. Thinks in families and goals such as college or retirement, not account numbers. Needs quarterly reports for dozens of clients at a time.
t.advisor.tx2b551: Firm super admin“I want to pre-set the default dashboards for all advisors at my firm, so that I can control what my advisors see.”
t.advisor.tx5746f: Platform operationsOnboards new advisory firms: colours, logo, disclosures, default reports. Before this work, that meant engineering tickets.
t.advisor.txac09a: What the legacy product got wrong, ranked by severity
t.advisor.tx7c261: Severity uses Nielsen’s scale: 3 blocks or misleads, 2 is minor but frequent, 1 is cosmetic. This table set the order of work for the year.
t.advisor.tx21a14: Clients and accounts are separate flat lists. No household or goal view exists.
t.advisor.tx9334c: Batch reporting spans two dialogs, three tabs, a dual list with arrow buttons, then a separate status page.
t.advisor.txcfd72: Batch status sits in a colour heatmap far from the report row. Failures are easy to miss.
t.advisor.tx860cc: Report templates and firm branding can only be changed by engineering.
t.advisor.tx0ff3e: Every database field is a column, with equal visual weight.
t.advisor.txedac9: Placeholder values (01/01/1900, “AcctNum”) look like real data.
t.advisor.tx1ff66: Toolbar icons are inconsistent across screens, and some actions hide in drop-downs.
t.advisor.tx40a88: No undo after starting a long-running batch job.
t.advisor.tx19a3f: One pattern library, so learning one screen teaches the rest
t.advisor.txd6bad: The biggest UI change was consistency, not polish. A small set of patterns ran through all four modules and gave engineering reusable components.
t.advisor.tx86859: My part: tokens, components and tables
t.advisor.txfda88: I built a major part of the design system: the token structure behind every firm’s theme, the core components, and the table patterns that most screens depend on.
t.advisor.txad63c: TokensThree tiers. Primitives feed semantic tokens, which feed components, so white-label themes change in one place.
t.advisor.tx1956b: TablesOne table, used everywhere. Households, accounts, documents and firms all share this anatomy.
t.advisor.tx38b1d: Fixing the menu with card sorting
t.advisor.txf6f5f: Advisors kept getting lost in the navigation: items were named after database objects and jobs, not the work. I ran an open card sort with advisors and admins, then regrouped and renamed the menu following Nielsen’s heuristic match between system and the real world.
t.advisor.tx281a7: Card sortFrom system words to advisor groups. Four groups that mirror how advisors talk about their week.
t.advisor.txb0fbb: StitcherReport stitcher, under Report builder
t.advisor.tx2fa27: Sketches are recreated to illustrate the work; token names show the structure rather than the exact production values.
t.advisor.tx512eb: Page frameGlobal search, an expanding icon rail, breadcrumbs, a title and a shared legal footer on every screen.
t.advisor.txa4ece: Entity headerAvatar or icon, name, and one line of key facts. Used for household, account and firm alike.
t.advisor.tx55122: Data tableCheckboxes, sortable headers, a linked primary column, row actions and numbered pagination.
t.advisor.txdefab: Table toolbarPrimary action on the left; Download, Customize and Filter on the right, always in that order.
t.advisor.tx4a4c6: Status languagePercentage and spinner, quiet check, red text with an icon. Colour is never the only signal.
t.advisor.tx8f8f8: Visual toneNeutral grey canvas, white surfaces, red for actions and black for structure. Gradients and bevels removed.
t.advisor.tx53c4a: Google’s HEART framework, with one signal and one metric per dimension, so each projection can be checked against real data.
t.advisor.tx5a818: HappinessAdvisors feel in control at quarter-end.SUS and a one-question CSAT after a batch run.
t.advisor.txa44c6: EngagementThe household view becomes home.Share of sessions starting on household details.
t.advisor.tx12e4a: AdoptionFirms use the builder and self-serve setup.Firms with a custom page or theme within 30 days.
t.advisor.tx0f1ac: RetentionSaved filters are reused each quarter.Saved-filter reuse rate across quarters.
t.advisor.tx5181a: Task successBatches finish without help.Completion rate, time on task, error-to-retry time.
t.advisor.tx65993: What I learned, and what I’d do next
t.advisor.txa1ef0: Design for the mental model, map to the data model. Households and goals were groupings of data that already existed. Reframing the UI, not the schema, kept engineering cost low and the change large for users.
t.advisor.tx2b22c: Split complex tools by role. Separating Page Builder from Report Stitcher gave each audience a simple tool instead of one tool that suits nobody.
t.advisor.tx8de08: Measure from day one. Next time I’d agree baseline metrics before design starts, so outcomes like these could be stated as facts.

t.advisor.txeb276: Make the contrast check blocking, and add colour-blind-safe chart palettes
t.advisor.tx2c7e9: Instrument the HEART metrics in the documents centre
t.advisor.tx00ef3: Screens are from the engagement and shown for portfolio purposes. Client and investor data in legacy screenshots has been blurred. Outcome figures are labelled projections.

t.agrifunds.txb4f6e: AgriFunds: one customer view for farm lenders, in place of four systems
t.agrifunds.tx82e01: Loan officers and service staff at a network of agricultural lending associations had to jump between a loan system, a core banking system, a CRM and a statements tool to help one farmer. I designed the portal that brings a customer, their loans and their borrowing entities into one place.
t.agrifunds.tx5be7d: Research, UX/UI, specs and design QA
t.agrifunds.tx42426: Drag to compare. The legacy loan screen hid each topic behind its own tab; the redesign shows the loan in context of the customer and their other loans. Names in the legacy screenshot are blurred.
t.agrifunds.txa1019: From four systems to one customer view
t.agrifunds.tx1d24f: 4 → 1loan, core banking, CRM and statements tools brought into one portal
t.agrifunds.tx6acae: 5modules designed end to end, from customer hub to creating a borrowing entity
t.agrifunds.txff6fc: 11 → 4tabs on a customer, down from eleven on the legacy loan screen
t.agrifunds.tx8896f: 1shared set of specs and components the developers built from
t.agrifunds.txd94ab: Customer, loan and entity data lived in separate systems with different names for the same things, so simple requests took many screens.
t.agrifunds.tx86aba: Audit every legacy screen, agree one vocabulary with subject experts, then design module by module with specs and design QA.
t.agrifunds.txed9db: A single customer view with a pinned header, four tabs, and guided flows for editing details and creating borrowing entities.
t.agrifunds.tx07353: Farm lending runs on relationships, and on many systems
t.agrifunds.tx57916: AgriFunds serves a network of local agricultural lending associations. A farmer may hold several loans through one or more borrowing entities, such as a family farm or a partnership, each with its own members, notes and equity.
t.agrifunds.tx14b01: To answer one call, staff looked up the customer in one system, the loans in another, statements in a third and notes in a CRM, each with its own layout and terms.
t.agrifunds.tx2adf2: BeforeLegacy loan system. Eleven tabs and dense tables for one customer.
t.agrifunds.tx7e31e: BeforeLegacy statements tool. Statements lived in yet another tool.
t.agrifunds.txc8153: Four systems to answer one customer question
t.agrifunds.tx590ed: Different names for the same field in each system
t.agrifunds.tx892f3: No clear view of which entity a loan belongs to
t.agrifunds.txbe94a: Hard to tell which system a piece of data came from
t.agrifunds.txff445: Creating a borrowing entity relied on memory and manual checks
t.agrifunds.tx672cb: Retire screen-hopping and give every association one consistent way to serve members.
t.agrifunds.tx8d739: See the customer, their loans and entities in one place, and act without switching systems.
t.agrifunds.txaeaa3: Show where each value comes from, so fixes land in the right source system.
t.agrifunds.txc23ca: Loan officerManages a book of farm customers. Needs the whole relationship, loans, entities and equity, before a conversation.
t.agrifunds.txd5e6a: Customer service representativeAnswers calls about payments and statements. Needs quick answers and safe edits to contact details.
t.agrifunds.tx47c81: Operations staffSet up and maintain borrowing entities and roles. Need guided steps and protection from duplicates.
t.agrifunds.tx593b8: Learning the business through its old screens
t.agrifunds.tx33093: Legacy screen auditMapped every field and tab across the loan system, core banking, CRM and statements tools, module by module.
t.agrifunds.tx2c417: Subject-expert sessionsWalkthroughs with lending and servicing experts to learn how each screen is really used and what can be retired.
t.agrifunds.txaf81e: Data dictionaryBuilt with the business: each system field, its plain-language label and its meaning, so the new screens speak one language.
t.agrifunds.tx0f0f3: Requirement reviewsTurned written requirements into wireframes for each module and agreed them with product owners before visual design.
t.agrifunds.txb6c01: Walkthrough testingReviewed prototypes with staff and product owners, then folded feedback into the next iteration.
t.agrifunds.tx1e03e: ResearchData dictionary. System fields mapped to plain labels and meanings.
t.agrifunds.tx591b7: ResearchField audit. Every legacy block reviewed: keep, merge or retire.
t.agrifunds.txca3ee: What we learned, and the principle each one became
t.agrifunds.txf2922: Staff think in customers and relationships, while the old systems were organised by data tables. The new portal had to start from the customer.
t.agrifunds.tx24679: Context is lost when switching screensA customer header pinned on every tab
t.agrifunds.tx44e99: Same field, different namesOne vocabulary from the data dictionary
t.agrifunds.txc8be5: Loans feel disconnected from entitiesGroup loans under their borrowing entity
t.agrifunds.txab053: Unsure where data came fromSource tags on every row
t.agrifunds.txd2c43: Accidental edits and duplicatesSeparate read and edit modes, and duplicate checks
t.agrifunds.tx44da8: Pick a module to see the screens and the decisions behind them.
t.agrifunds.tx59574: One place to start every task.
t.agrifunds.tx0a427: Roles, notes and equity in one view.
t.agrifunds.tx974ff: A guided flow with safe checks.
t.agrifunds.tx724f1: Customer hub: what can I do for this customer?
t.agrifunds.tx69709: FinalCustomer hub. Every task for a customer, grouped by the team that owns it.
t.agrifunds.tx1ec93: Persistent customer headerName, IDs, address, contact, loan count and lending association stay pinned on every tab, with source system links on the right.
t.agrifunds.txda46e: Four tabs in the order of the workActions, Customer Details, BEs and Loans. The order came from design QA with the business.
t.agrifunds.tx71696: Actions grouped by teamCards for digital banking, cash services, teller, equity, pricing, credit and shared services replace menus spread across systems.
t.agrifunds.txcf542: Filter instead of huntingType an action or task to narrow the cards.
t.agrifunds.tx99183: Shortcuts on every tabFavourite, customise, print and help, always in the same place.
t.agrifunds.tx9bf31: Customer details: one record, many sources
t.agrifunds.tx04dc6: FinalRead-only view. Overview, contact and statements on one scroll.
t.agrifunds.tx1fa2b: FinalEdit an individual. Fields change with the customer type.
t.agrifunds.txb6b7c: FinalEdit an organisation. Farming-specific fields such as year began farming.
t.agrifunds.txf4e9b: Read and edit are separate modesStaff browse safely and switch to “Modify customer details” only when they mean to change something.
t.agrifunds.txf3b2f: Individual or organisationThe form adapts: SSN and birth date for a person; tax ID, organisation type and year began farming for a business.
t.agrifunds.tx0a18e: Source on every rowTags show which system each address, phone or email came from, so staff know where a fix will land.
t.agrifunds.tx8df21: Sub-tabs for long recordsAll, Overview, Contact and Statements keep a long profile scannable.
t.agrifunds.tx6575e: Statements in contextAnnual statements and billing notices sit with the customer, grouped by borrowing entity.

t.agrifunds.tx402a9: Left rail grouped by entityLoans sit under the borrowing entity they belong to, with purpose, status and source on each card.
t.agrifunds.txd5b86: Summary firstLoan and billing summary opens by default, so staff see the whole relationship before drilling in.
t.agrifunds.tx580db: Closed loans on demandA toggle hides closed loans until they are needed.
t.agrifunds.tx292ae: Plain-language labelsField names were rewritten from system codes into lending terms using the data dictionary.
t.agrifunds.txb929a: Past due made visibleDays and occurrences past due get their own block instead of hiding in a tab.
t.agrifunds.txfdd15: Borrowing entities: who is on the loan, and how
t.agrifunds.txaa51e: FinalBorrowing entity details. Overview, roles, notes, equity and tax data for one entity.
t.agrifunds.tx156ac: Entities listed beside detailsSwitch between a customer’s borrowing entities without leaving the page.
t.agrifunds.txc80ea: Roles as a tablePrimary, member, voter and alternate stockowner, each linked to the customer record.
t.agrifunds.tx23a0f: Notes with their loansExpandable rows show which loans sit under each note.
t.agrifunds.txe475b: Equity and tax togetherEquity balance, equity codes and IRS reportable data in one scroll.
t.agrifunds.tx2d4c1: Create a borrowing entity: guided, validated, recoverable
t.agrifunds.tx5b5d4: FinalStep 1. Start with the overview.
t.agrifunds.tx0d48e: FinalStep 2. Add roles, notes and equity codes.
t.agrifunds.txcd5f4: FinalStep 3. Confirmation with the next steps.
t.agrifunds.tx37d9a: FinalDuplicate check. Stops a duplicate before it is created.

t.agrifunds.txe97aa: Toggles for yes-or-no codesEquity codes default to No and switch with one tap.
t.agrifunds.txc35ef: Duplicate preventionIf the branch already has an entity with the same roles, a dialog links straight to it.

t.agrifunds.tx51e8e: Specs the developers could build from
t.agrifunds.txc56b8: Every screen shipped with a visual spec: spacing, type sizes and the shared component class to use, such as agf-table large, agf-table medium, agf-calendar and agf-button-primary-round-fill.
t.agrifunds.tx6102c: SpecEdit mode spec. Spacing of 8, 12, 16, 24 and 32, and the component for each table.
t.agrifunds.tx8f89f: SpecRead mode spec. The same rhythm in read mode, so switching feels seamless.

t.agrifunds.tx14267: Table sizesLarge for addresses, medium for phone and email, with columns aligned to the labels above.
t.agrifunds.tx85d64: One button systemFilled for the main action, outlined for the secondary, always bottom right.

t.agrifunds.txb602e: QAHeader review. Icon size, link colour and spacing fixes.
t.agrifunds.tx3076e: QATab order. Tabs reordered to follow the work.
t.agrifunds.txc8a28: Vocabulary is design. Agreeing one name for each field did more for clarity than any layout change.
t.agrifunds.txf365d: Show the source. In consolidated systems, people trust data more when they can see where it came from.
t.agrifunds.tx798c6: Specs and QA close the loop. Redlines and numbered review notes kept the build true to the design.

t.aster.txc2faa: Aster Bank: eLearning that shows wealth teams a better working day
t.aster.txb9066: An international bank in Singapore was rolling out a new way of working for its wealth management teams. I designed the UI of the eLearning modules that introduced it: a course player and a set of illustrated screens that follow one relationship manager through his day, before and after the change.
t.aster.tx94adc: A change programme explained as one person’s working day
t.aster.txbff06: 15short screens per module, each carrying a single idea
t.aster.tx35236: 1relationship manager, Kevin, whose day carries the whole story
t.aster.txd5e8e: 3help tools on every screen: Resource, Glossary and Help
t.aster.tx2511f: A new way of working for wealth teams is hard to explain in slides and policy documents. People needed to see why it mattered to their own day.
t.aster.txd9848: Tell it as a story. Follow one relationship manager through a familiar day, show the friction, then show the same day with the new workbench.
t.aster.txa56ad: A consistent course player and a flat, illustrated screen system the learning team could reuse across modules.
t.aster.tx95519: A transformation that people had to understand, not just attend
t.aster.txa5447: The bank’s wealth management business was moving its relationship managers onto a new workbench: one place for portfolio performance, reports, appointments, calls and events, with research and portfolio reporting built in.
t.aster.tx67520: Training had to reach busy front-line staff, so it needed to be short, self-paced and clear about the benefit before it asked anyone to learn a new tool.
t.aster.tx78545: An abstract change programme with many moving parts
t.aster.tx93125: Busy staff with little time for training
t.aster.txc077c: Banking terms that newer staff might not know
t.aster.tx60cd8: Several modules that had to look and work alike
t.aster.txe5318: Help wealth teams understand and adopt the new way of working.
t.aster.tx91f8c: Quickly see what changes in my day and why it is better.
t.aster.tx33d0d: One player and one visual language that every module can reuse.
t.aster.tx26eee: Relationship managers and the teams around them
t.aster.tx4ef93: The learners were the people who would use the workbench every day, so the story had to look and sound like their own desk, their own clients and their own to-do list.
t.aster.txb35c2: Show the day, then show the difference
t.aster.tx5c112: A persona to followKevin, a relationship manager, gives learners someone to recognise. Every screen is a moment in his day.
t.aster.tx29bc2: Familiar momentsMarket research, today’s tasks, a client who wants to invest in real estate, a pile of client files: the everyday work the change affects.
t.aster.tx8f7f3: Before and afterThe same desk shown twice. Before: manual effort, collating reports, coordinating over calls and emails. After: information anytime and anywhere, automated tasks, more time for clients.
t.aster.txc09a7: The tool, in contextThe workbench appears as Kevin’s own checklist, ticking off portfolio performance and appointments against today’s tasks.
t.aster.tx11b42: Short screensOne idea per screen and a visible page count, so learners always know how far they have to go.
t.aster.tx6b35e: Eight beats, sketched before any screen was drawn
t.aster.tx22301: I storyboarded the module as a sequence of beats, so the learning team could agree on the story and the order before visual design began.
t.aster.txa49db: StoryboardOne module, one working day. The new tool only appears once the pain has been felt.
t.aster.txd67b9: A frame that stays still so the story can move
t.aster.txf5479: Every module runs inside the same player. Controls never move, so learners spend their attention on the scene, not on finding the next button.
t.aster.tx3a15e: WireframePlayer anatomy. Title and menu on top, help one tap away, progress at the bottom.
t.aster.txbebc8: Learners lose their placePage count and a segmented progress bar on every screen
t.aster.txa96e6: Banking terms slow new staff downGlossary always in the top bar
t.aster.txd8874: Some learners use touch screensA swipe hint and large, simple targets
t.aster.tx61295: Learners want to keep notesA notes button in the same corner on every screen
t.aster.tx61eb9: Flat illustration, one desk, a few strong colours
t.aster.tx724cb: A top-down view of Kevin’s desk is the recurring stage: the same monitor, keyboard, notebook and plant, so learners always know where they are. Vignette cards titled “Today at Kevin’s desk” zoom into single moments, each in one dominant colour.
t.aster.txcee6b: FinalThe stage. Kevin’s desk, seen from above.
t.aster.tx045ed: FinalA vignette. One moment, one colour, one caption.
t.aster.txcbae4: FinalEnable the transformation. The opening sets the theme.
t.aster.tx506a2: FinalIntroduction video. A short video sets up the story.
t.aster.tx72ebe: FinalToday and tomorrow. Kevin’s to-do list, in his words.
t.aster.tx28274: FinalA client calls. A real request that needs data fast.
t.aster.tx1c262: FinalThe paperwork. Where the old way slows him down.
t.aster.txe36fc: FinalBack at the desk. The stage returns between moments.
t.aster.tx0a2c5: BeforeBefore. Manual effort, collating reports, chasing calls and emails.
t.aster.tx42860: AfterAfter. The same desk, with the work automated.
t.aster.tx6e2a4: FinalThe tools. Each capability introduced as a card.
t.aster.tx4e3f8: FinalWorkbench 1.1. Today’s tasks, ticked off in the new tool.
t.aster.txd02ef: Story before software. Learners meet the problem in Kevin’s day before they meet the tool.
t.aster.tx39122: One idea per screen. A headline, one illustration and a one-line caption.
t.aster.tx639d2: Familiar over flashy. Real tasks and real requests from a relationship manager’s week.
t.aster.tx07692: Colour with a job. Dark for the old way, bright for the new; each vignette owns one colour.
t.aster.tx05ca0: A frame that never moves. The same player and controls in every module.
t.aster.txc0c33: What I learned, and what I’d add next
t.aster.txd63b9: Training is a product too. The same UX basics apply: know the learner, cut the noise, show progress.
t.aster.tx2b588: Stories travel. A single persona made an abstract programme easy to explain across teams.
t.aster.txd6ab6: Next, I’d add practice. A short scenario where learners complete Kevin’s tasks in the workbench themselves.
t.aster.txee13c: And measure it. Completion rates and a quick confidence check before and after each module.

t.autolore.tx8b8f6: AutoLore: a touch kiosk that lets classic cars tell their own stories
t.autolore.tx97fe3: A private collection of around 50 classic cars became a public museum in Florida. I designed the kiosk that stands in front of each car, turning a founder’s memories and hundreds of scattered artefacts into stories any visitor can explore.
t.autolore.tx76013: Every car on the floor now has a story to tell
t.autolore.tx9f936: ~50classic cars, each with its own kiosk story
t.autolore.tx4316a: 3ways into every car: its stories, a gallery and its specifications
t.autolore.txd994c: 2+years in use and still growing, as new stories are added
t.autolore.tx5913e: The cars’ histories lived in the founder’s memory and in hundreds of uncatalogued artefacts. None of it was ready for the public.
t.autolore.tx61156: Study the museum and its visitors, map the walk through the halls, then design a kiosk simple enough for anyone to use standing in front of a car.
t.autolore.tx357d0: A dark, story-first kiosk with one clear path per car, backed by a content system so the team can keep adding stories.
t.autolore.tx01d31: “You have done an excellent job on this project! I feel, as does the client, that the designs are excellent and will bring to life the content we wish to present on such historical cars.”
t.autolore.tx27362: From a private passion to a public museum
t.autolore.tx48b71: The founder had collected around 50 cars over a lifetime and decided to open a museum in Jacksonville, Florida, to share them with the public. Every car came with its own history, memories and people.
t.autolore.tx254b7: Hundreds of artefacts about the cars sat in different places and had never been catalogued. Much of the story existed only in the founder’s mind and the minds of a few others.
t.autolore.tx176b0: No catalogue of the artefacts, photos and documents
t.autolore.tx7c023: Stories held in people’s memories, not in writing
t.autolore.tx9e843: Each story could be about a person, a car or a technical breakthrough
t.autolore.tx756cf: Content had to live online and appear on a screen beside each car
t.autolore.tx7ee0f: Visitors of every age and ability, with no instructions
t.autolore.tx51bbd: Bring the collection to life and give every car a voice on the museum floor.
t.autolore.txd403c: Walk up to any car and quickly discover why it matters.
t.autolore.tx69740: Collect, organise and publish stories in a system the team can keep updating.
t.autolore.tx94626: Designing for everyone who walks in
t.autolore.tx2d6ba: A museum is a public place, so anyone could be the user: there is no login, no training and no second chance at a first impression.
t.autolore.tx4e361: Understanding the space before designing the screen
t.autolore.txe4e07: In public places, the environment shapes the experience as much as the interface does.
t.autolore.txa8bf0: Stakeholder interviewsConversations with the founder and his team to capture the stories, priorities and the people behind each car.
t.autolore.tx96c03: Environment studyLight, mood, location and temperature on the museum floor, which set screen brightness, contrast and theme.
t.autolore.txe3d7b: Comparative reviewCase studies of kiosks and apps in other public places, to learn what helps people succeed without help.
t.autolore.txd343d: Journey mappingThe visitor’s walk through the halls, step by step, to place the kiosk where curiosity peaks.
t.autolore.tx149cd: Content auditWorking with a business analyst to sort the artefacts into stories, captions and specifications.
t.autolore.tx0cc71: Curiosity peaks in front of a car
t.autolore.txb9406: The journey map showed the moment that matters: a visitor stops at a car and wants to know more. That is where the kiosk stands, in both the Forerunners and the Frontrunners halls.
t.autolore.txda18c: Arrive at the museumCurious, getting oriented
t.autolore.tx37baa: Enter the Forerunners hallWonder at the earliest cars
t.autolore.txc561c: Look at the carsWants the story behind one
t.autolore.tx46fcd: Use the kiosk by a carStory, gallery and specs
t.autolore.txd6457: Enter the Frontrunners hallRacing-era cars
t.autolore.txdd3f2: Look at the carsCompares eras
t.autolore.tx03baf: Use the kiosk againAlready knows how it works
t.autolore.txb6fc5: LeaveRemembers a story, not a label
t.autolore.tx8d041: Each kiosk opens on its car. From there, a visitor can read its stories, browse its gallery or check its specifications, and always find their way back.
t.autolore.tx2d6f5: What the research told us to do
t.autolore.tx6fb27: Visitors stand, glance and move onOne car per kiosk, with the story told in short screens
t.autolore.txa0fcd: Museum halls are dim and dramaticA dark theme that cuts glare and lets the photos glow
t.autolore.tx6dd82: Nobody reads instructionsA single “Next” and three large icons, the same on every screen
t.autolore.txd54d0: People like to know how much is leftA vertical progress rail showing where they are in the story
t.autolore.tx80213: Stories are about people, not just machinesArchive photos and captions alongside the specifications
t.autolore.tx08867: Shaping the story flow in mid-fidelity
t.autolore.tx7d47b: Working with the business analyst, I sketched wireframes and carved the content into a journey: an introduction, the machine’s unique features, and the facts behind its acquisition.
t.autolore.txa03b3: WireframeIntroduction. Title, a short intro and a sound to play.
t.autolore.txb28a3: WireframeUniqueness of the machine. Key facts as short bullets.
t.autolore.tx55b4f: WireframeFacts behind the acquisition. The rail shows the story is nearly done.
t.autolore.txf86b6: A dark, cinematic kiosk that puts the car first
t.autolore.tx444f6: FinalIntroduction. A bold title and one line on why the car matters.
t.autolore.tx046ca: FinalThe story. Short paragraphs with an archive photo.
t.autolore.tx45ecc: FinalDesign specifications. Gold labels make the facts easy to scan.
t.autolore.txdc138: FinalGallery. Swipe through photos and videos.
t.autolore.txb99c6: In useBeside the car. Each kiosk stands next to the car it describes.
t.autolore.txd491a: In useThe kiosk. At standing height, angled for easy reach.
t.autolore.tx76180: Easy for a child, a grandparent or a wheelchair user
t.autolore.tx6db72: Large touch targetsRound icons and a wide Next button that are easy to hit, standing or seated.
t.autolore.tx069f9: High contrastWhite and gold text on a dark background, readable under museum lighting.
t.autolore.txcfd8f: Short, plain languageStories broken into brief screens that work for younger readers and tourists.
t.autolore.tx0815d: Predictable layoutThe same controls in the same places on every car, so learning one kiosk means knowing them all.
t.autolore.tx52c5c: More than textPhotos, video and engine sounds for visitors who prefer to look and listen.
t.autolore.txc0c33: What I learned, and what I’d add next
t.autolore.tx576a1: Context is the brief. Light, mood and how people move through a hall decided more of the design than any style guide.
t.autolore.txe02f7: Content design is UX. Turning memories and artefacts into short stories was as important as the screens themselves.
t.autolore.tx9a1e9: Next, I’d measure it. Dwell time and the most-read stories would show which cars spark the most curiosity.
t.autolore.tx320b9: And widen the audience. Audio narration, captions on video and other languages would welcome even more visitors.

t.finguard.txeb9af: Case study · Banking · Financial crime compliance
t.finguard.tx6da8a: FinGuard: helping bank investigators see risk, and the reason for it, at a glance
t.finguard.tx8d132: A case management platform for a bank’s financial intelligence unit. I designed how analysts triage alerts, search across customers and accounts, and decide on a case from a single risk profile.
t.finguard.txa9be6: From scattered checks to one explainable view of customer risk
t.finguard.tx0d1ff: 5risk dimensions behind one score: attribute, watchlist, negative news, network and activity
t.finguard.txc1cb7: 3record types in one search: customers, alerts and cases, and accounts
t.finguard.txfb2dd: 1page to decide on a customer, with evidence, documents and audit trail
t.finguard.txb3411: Analysts had to clear alerts against regulatory deadlines while risk signals, documents and history lived in different places.
t.finguard.txdb32d: Map the investigation workflow with the people who do it, then design around their real decision: close, escalate or open a case.
t.finguard.tx0ad42: A dashboard, search and risk profile that show not only how risky a customer is, but why, with every change recorded.
t.finguard.txb27a0: High stakes, tight deadlines, many systems
t.finguard.tx25228: Banks must spot money laundering and fraud, know who their customers are, and prove to regulators how every decision was made. Inside the bank, a financial intelligence unit (FIU) reviews alerts raised by monitoring systems, carries out customer due diligence, and escalates suspicious activity.
t.finguard.tx98ca4: FinGuard brought that work into one tool: alerts, cases, onboarding reviews and periodic reviews, each scored for risk.
t.finguard.txd6767: Risk signals spread across watchlists, news, KYC files and transaction data
t.finguard.tx6b13a: A score with no explanation, which analysts could not defend
t.finguard.txcbff2: Deadlines on every alert and review, with aging hard to see
t.finguard.txeb071: Manual search for a customer’s other accounts and open items
t.finguard.txd3622: Quality checks done after the fact, in separate reports
t.finguard.txb7744: Clear more alerts on time without lowering the quality of decisions.
t.finguard.txfdf7c: Reach a defensible decision on a customer quickly, with the evidence in front of me.
t.finguard.tx87d21: Every score, document and change must be explainable and traceable.
t.finguard.txd1839: FIU analystWorks an assigned queue of alerts and cases every day. Needs to know which customer to open first, and to see the evidence behind a score before closing or escalating it.
t.finguard.tx77f5e: Quality reviewerSamples completed work against quality KPIs. Needs to retrace what an analyst saw and changed, and when.
t.finguard.txd8076: Team leadBalances workload across analysts. Needs volume, aging and quality trends on one screen to spot bottlenecks before deadlines slip.
t.finguard.txbba1d: Learning the investigation, not just the interface
t.finguard.txaab27: Financial crime teams handle confidential data and work to strict procedures, so research had to respect both: masked or sample data only, sessions scheduled around queue deadlines, and compliance in the room.
t.finguard.tx8b85b: Compliance leadership, quality assurance and technology, to understand regulatory obligations, KPIs and data sources.
t.finguard.tx7d844: Observing analysts work real alerts end to end, noting every system, tab and spreadsheet they touched.
t.finguard.txa4e3e: Breaking an investigation into steps, decisions and hand-offs, from alert to disposition.
t.finguard.txa4a28: Existing alert reports, case notes and KYC checklists, to learn the vocabulary users already trust.
t.finguard.txb1c09: Three roles and the alert lifecycle, shared with stakeholders to agree what to fix first.
t.finguard.tx5f94a: Clickable prototypes with sample customers, testing whether analysts could explain a score and find related accounts.
t.finguard.tx46228: Sketches are recreated to illustrate each activity; quotes are paraphrased and no customer data is shown.
t.finguard.txca3ee: What we learned, and the principle each one became
t.finguard.tx189fb: Analysts didn’t need more data. They needed to see why a customer was risky, in a way they could defend to a reviewer or a regulator.
t.finguard.txb202b: A single score hides its causesBreak risk into five named dimensions, each with its own evidence
t.finguard.txaa010: Analysts open the wrong case firstRank the queue by risk and due date, with status in the row
t.finguard.tx7e6e6: Related accounts and items are found by handOne search that returns customers, items and accounts together
t.finguard.tx7d39c: Reviewers can’t retrace decisionsA change log and risk history on every profile
t.finguard.tx882a4: Leads learn about backlogs too lateAging and quality on the dashboard, next to volume
t.finguard.tx2b615: Three screens that follow the investigation
t.finguard.txc08f1: Triage on the dashboard, find everything with search, decide on the profile. Numbers on each screen match the notes beside it.
t.finguard.tx63991: Workload, aging, quality and a risk-ranked queue.
t.finguard.tx55f31: One query across entities, items and accounts.
t.finguard.txb104d: The score, the evidence and the audit trail.
t.finguard.txbb914: Analyst dashboard: what needs me first?
t.finguard.tx38feb: FinalAnalyst dashboard. Workload, aging and quality up top; a risk-ranked queue below.
t.finguard.tx20d4a: Workload at a glanceItems by status shows how much is open this month and how much is closed.
t.finguard.txb521b: Aging by work typeHours outstanding for alerts, cases, onboarding reviews and periodic reviews, so nothing quietly breaches its deadline.
t.finguard.txfc520: Quality score by KPITeam leads see quality trends next to volume, not in a separate report.
t.finguard.txe1194: Cases and alerts as tabsCounts on each tab tell analysts how big each queue is before they open it.
t.finguard.tx693b2: Risk DNA stripFive small bars, one per risk dimension, show why a customer scored high without opening the profile.
t.finguard.tx52b0e: Score with a wordEvery score carries High, Medium or Low in text, so colour is never the only signal.
t.finguard.tx1b845: Status and due date in the rowAwaiting documentation, DD research or newly assigned, with open and due dates to sort by urgency.
t.finguard.txab4d6: Advanced search: everything about this customer
t.finguard.tx0743a: FinalAdvanced search. One query, results grouped by entities, items and accounts.
t.finguard.txb3772: One search box, everywhereName, case or account number from the header, with Advanced Search one click away.
t.finguard.tx2d3fc: Facets in banking languagePersonal or business account; money market, savings, checking, deposit or certificate; alert, case, onboarding or periodic review; structuring or foreign transaction.
t.finguard.txf9611: Entities firstEvery record for a person in one table, with the review type (risk DNA, CDD or EDD) shown on each row.
t.finguard.tx639ec: Related itemsOpen alerts and cases for the same person, with their risk bars, status, due date and owner.
t.finguard.txda58d: Related accountsAccount type, relationship manager, address, tax ID and whether the account is active.
t.finguard.txd6160: A clear action on every rowView or Open, always in the last column, so the next step is never hidden.
t.finguard.txa4385: Entity risk profile: is this customer a risk, and why?
t.finguard.tx3ad69: FinalEntity risk profile. Everything an investigator needs to decide, on one page.
t.finguard.txd2bc8: Risk cardInitials, a score of 95 and the words High Risk on a calm deep-teal card, with previous and next to move through a queue. The number and label carry the risk, so the card itself doesn’t need to alarm.
t.finguard.txb491e: Associated accountsEvery account the customer holds, so investigators see the whole relationship.
t.finguard.tx6e919: Document centreKYC intake, driving licence and passport with upload dates and a clear validated switch; Notes and Tasks sit beside it.
t.finguard.tx173b8: Five risk dimensionsAttribute, watchlist, negative news, network and activity risk, each a tab with its own segmented bar.
t.finguard.txfd86e: Evidence, not just a scoreThe attribute tab lists what drove the score: name and address variations, phone and email checks, home-to-bank distance. The factor in question is outlined.
t.finguard.tx283b6: Risk over timeA trend line shows when risk rose, not only where it is today.
t.finguard.txf81f6: Change logWho changed what and when, ready for audit.
t.finguard.tx94fe2: Save and reprocessAnalysts can refresh the score after adding evidence, without leaving the page.
t.finguard.txbaaf1: Risk colours are reservedRed flags high risk; teal carries focus and medium risk; structure stays in greys and black.
t.finguard.tx1387f: Dense, but scannableExperts read tables all day, so rows are compact with clear labels, generous line spacing and right-hand actions.
t.finguard.tx412d5: One accent for actionTeal marks the active tab and the primary buttons, a calm, trustworthy banking tone that keeps the next step easy to find.
t.finguard.tx4f5c5: Built for auditors as much as for analysts
t.finguard.tx94384: Explainable scoresEvery score breaks down into dimensions and named factors an analyst can cite.
t.finguard.tx05872: Audit trailThe change log records the user, the action and the date on every profile.
t.finguard.tx2798c: Document validationKYC files show who uploaded them, when, and whether they were validated.
t.finguard.txa5ad9: Due diligence levelsRecords show the review type, such as customer or enhanced due diligence, so the right checks are applied.
t.finguard.txfa9fb: Not colour aloneRisk is shown with numbers and words as well as colour, for accessibility and for printed evidence packs.
t.finguard.tx12e4d: Privacy in researchPrototypes and tests used sample data, never real customer records.
t.finguard.tx876e5: The metrics a financial crime team cares about
t.finguard.txcf323: These are the signals I’d track to prove the design worked, each tied to a goal above.
t.finguard.tx0264b: SpeedAnalysts reach a decision faster.Average time from opening an alert to disposition.
t.finguard.tx20ab5: TimelinessFewer items breach their deadline.Share of alerts and reviews closed within SLA; aging hours by type.
t.finguard.tx52fed: QualityDecisions hold up on review.Quality score pass rate and rework rate.
t.finguard.txb1240: ConfidenceAnalysts can explain a score.Task success in usability tests; post-task confidence rating.
t.finguard.txa3bfd: EfficiencyLess hunting across systems.Searches and screens per investigation.
t.finguard.tx30506: What I learned, and what I’d do today
t.finguard.tx2a599: Explainability is the feature. In regulated work, a number without a reason is a liability. Designing the “why” mattered more than the score itself.
t.finguard.txc79b1: Design for the reviewer too. The audit trail and risk history turned a working tool into evidence a bank could stand behind.
t.finguard.txbdb3c: Today I’d raise contrast. Some light grey text on white would not pass WCAG 2.2 AA. I’d darken it and add pattern fills to the risk bars.
t.finguard.txb6217: And add assisted triage. With today’s AI, I’d explore summarising a customer’s risk in plain language, with the analyst always making the final call.

t.finunity.txef283: UX designer, from discovery to final UI
t.finunity.tx57998: I was one of two UX designers on the project, working with a business analyst and FinUnity’s stakeholders. Together we covered the whole design process:
t.finunity.tx5e268: Too many tools, none of them connected
t.finunity.txadf90: FinUnity is a tax financing company and a top choice for residential and commercial property owners in Texas, helping tens of thousands of Texans save their property from foreclosure. Its employees relied on many third-party applications that didn’t talk to each other. Agents re-entered information by hand and moved between systems constantly, so simple tasks took far longer than they should.
t.finunity.txe478f: Business processes out of step with the tools
t.finunity.tx06a4f: A single system that serves every segment of the business, with full coverage of loan and lien processes across CRM, underwriting, processing, servicing, the workflow engine and other modules.
t.finunity.txc225c: A heuristic evaluation set the agenda
t.finunity.txc0215: Before redesigning anything, we evaluated the legacy system against established usability heuristics. The main recommendation: build a system that is truly user-centred, with a strong user experience at its core.
t.finunity.tx91791: Annotated review of the legacy underwriting screen.
t.finunity.tx16f5e: Next and previous buttons were barely noticeable, so users couldn't tell what action they had just performed.
t.finunity.tx57c4b: The menu said “Landing” for what is known worldwide as a dashboard.
t.finunity.tx9b987: The view-history popup could only be closed with its small cross icon, not by clicking outside it.
t.finunity.txe33ce: Links looked like tabs, “Show Advanced Search” was styled differently again, and font sizes varied.
t.finunity.txb1907: Read-only fields could be edited by mistake with no warning message at all.
t.finunity.tx2615d: A search area carried over from the previous page was hard to recognise on the crowded screen.
t.finunity.tx6c755: The page was so busy that it was difficult to recognise and use.
t.finunity.txd4edb: Too much information on one page made it hard to perceive what mattered.
t.finunity.tx66dcb: There were no visual or documented hints to help people use the system.
t.finunity.tx0affb: How the findings shaped the design
t.finunity.txf9ec4: “Landing” in the menuUse the words people already know, like Dashboard
t.finunity.tx951bc: Inconsistent tabs, links and font sizesOne set of components and type sizes from the design system
t.finunity.txe71d7: Busy, crowded screensClear hierarchy that puts the next task first
t.finunity.txead54: No feedback after actionsVisible status for every task and action
t.finunity.tx2ed77: Learning the business, side by side with users
t.finunity.tx8e29b: Once the statement of work was signed, we studied the existing systems, use cases and stories. We then ran a one-week workshop at the client’s office in Dallas, Texas, to understand the business in depth, along with the users’ pain points, needs and system requirements.
t.finunity.tx5d74c: We picked FinUnity users of different ages and grouped them to build personas. Interviews about their pain points gave us a rich set of insights, and they were essential for designing a system that would also help FinUnity reach its business goals.
t.finunity.tx1e4da: Mapping the journey from acquisition to release
t.finunity.tx9c502: We combined in-person interviews, surveys and user reviews into a customer journey map. It showed the ideal journey for the new system and where the old one broke down, closed knowledge gaps between the team and stakeholders, and marked each touchpoint by intent and task, including people’s emotions and expectations.
t.finunity.tx96210: The loan and lien lifecycle, from acquisition to release.
t.finunity.txad705: Balancing user needs with business goals
t.finunity.txf46f3: With stakeholders, we sketched flows on paper, organised features on sticky notes and turned the strongest ideas into wireframes.
t.finunity.tx0e75d: We then built low-fidelity wireframes with the business analyst and the client, and tested them with users to validate our thinking before any visual design.
t.finunity.tx2f1c5: A design system to keep every module consistent
t.finunity.tx0664b: With many modules to cover, consistency had to be designed in. We built a design system of principles, brand guidelines, components and patterns, giving designers and developers a shared vocabulary and making the whole process more efficient.
t.finunity.tx38d5c: Evaluate before you redesign. The heuristic review gave everyone a shared, evidence-based list of problems to solve.
t.finunity.txa8ce4: Go where the work happens. A week on site with the people who use the system every day showed us more than any document could.
t.finunity.tx8dccf: Consistency scales. A design system kept many modules feeling like one product as the platform grew.

t.g.txe5672: Guru Samman SamarohEvent visualisation and design
t.guru.tx089e0: Guru Samman Samaroh 2019: designing a day to honour our teachers
t.guru.tx9b177: A full school ground, more than 300 guests, and the first alumni-led tribute in the school’s history. I visualised and designed every part of it, from the ground plan to the printed backdrop.
t.guru.tx353a5: Janta Inter College, Pokhrikhet, Pauri Garhwal
t.guru.tx8f8b1: A full ground and a proud moment for the school
t.guru.txdaf37: ~90days of planning, design and delivery, May to July 2019
t.guru.txde9fa: Everyartefact designed and printed by me, from ground plan to backdrop
t.guru.tx80033: Former and current students wanted to honour the teachers who shaped them, with an event worthy of the occasion.
t.guru.tx22aa7: Treat the ground like an interface: plan zones and paths first, visualise the whole setup, then design every piece people would see and touch.
t.guru.txf4ad2: A packed ground, teachers celebrated on stage, and a day enjoyed by teachers, students and families alike.
t.guru.tx71181: From a plan on paper to a full ground
t.guru.txc7fe7: The finished setup on the day: a stage for the honoured teachers, a red-carpet aisle, and waterproof shaded seating for everyone who came.
t.guru.txff579: An outdoor venue needed protection, so a waterproof shade covered the stage and every seat, with fans to keep guests comfortable.
t.guru.tx9e1a4: A grand red-carpet entrance, with stanchions and marigold garlands, so every teacher walked to the stage like a guest of honour.
t.guru.txbc518: Reserved, signed seating near the stage put the teachers at the centre of the day.
t.guru.tx1a7c5: PhotoThe stage. Senior teachers seated in front of the backdrop I designed, with marked seating for them in front of the stage.
t.guru.tx7782b: VisualisationThe setup, visualised. How the whole ground would come together, before anything was built.
t.guru.tx7ba72: Event visualisation and design, end to end
t.guru.txd1279: This was my first event design. As part of the alumni group organising the day, I owned how it would look and work, and saw every printed piece through to production. The work ran for about 90 days, from May to July 2019, with the event itself on 16 June.
t.guru.tx7ea8d: A first for the school, organised by its own students
t.guru.tx7687e: Guru Samman Samaroh means “a ceremony to honour our teachers”. It was organised by the school’s former and current students, the first time alumni had come together to do something like this in the school’s history.
t.guru.txdcd06: The venue was the school ground at Janta Inter College in Pokhrikhet, Pauri Garhwal: a hillside site bordered by a road, terraced fields and a stone wall. The audience would be broad, from senior teachers and their families to current students and villagers, so the space had to feel welcoming to everyone and still put the teachers clearly at its centre.
t.guru.txa5d53: Honour the teachers with dignity, so they feel celebrated from the moment they arrive.
t.guru.tx40212: 300+ people of every age: teachers, students, alumni, families and the local community.
t.guru.txa868a: An outdoor hillside ground in mid-June, open to sun and monsoon rain, so weather protection, clear paths and sightlines to the stage mattered.
t.guru.tx02881: Designing a space the way I design a product
t.guru.tx9716e: Deciding what goes where, before anything was built
t.guru.tx16fce: I started with the ground itself. The sketch maps the road, the terraced field and the stone wall, then places the stage, the VIP seating and the guest blocks around a single central aisle.
t.guru.tx2d605: PlanGround plan sketch. Zones, seating and paths, labelled.
t.guru.txc5f68: Stage against the back wallA solid wall behind the stage gave the backdrop a frame and kept every seat facing one focal point.
t.guru.tx59e39: A red-carpet welcomeA red carpet from the entrance steps straight to the stage, lined with gold stanchions and marigolds, gave the teachers a grand walk of honour, the kind of welcome usually reserved for big-city events, so they felt proud from the moment they arrived.
t.guru.txfcbe9: Raised VIP seating near the stageGuests of honour sat on the terrace beside the stage, close to the action and visible to the crowd.
t.guru.txa8aba: Guest blocks on both sidesRows either side of the aisle kept sightlines to the stage short and clear.
t.guru.txbe0e2: Safe and comfortable outdoorsBecause the event was in the open, I planned a waterproof shade over the stage and all the seating, with ceiling fans, so guests stayed protected from sun and rain.
t.guru.txf56e0: One look across print, décor and dress
t.guru.tx3703e: I designed and had printed every artefact guests would see, and planned a colour theme and dress code to go with them, so the day looked like one event rather than a collection of rented parts.
t.guru.txc0dda: Stage backdropAn emblem, the event name in Hindi with a decorative flourish, a credit to the former and current students, the date and the full venue name, set in deep blue on white.
t.guru.txf76b8: Posters and bannersAnnouncing the event to the school and the surrounding villages in the same style.
t.guru.tx9aaa1: Signage and place cardsHindi cards on the stanchions marked seating for teachers and senior teachers, so guests of honour were guided without needing to ask.
t.guru.tx5d85f: Dress codeA planned dress code for the organising team, so hosts were easy to spot and looked part of the same event as the stage and print.
t.guru.txa2fe3: One colour theme was planned for the whole event and carried through the stage, décor, print and dress code.
t.guru.tx10da1: A ground full of people, all facing the teachers
t.guru.tx43d64: On 16 June 2019 the ground filled with more than 300 people. Teachers, students and families sat on both sides of the aisle under the canopy, with more watching from the terraces, while the honoured teachers took their places on stage.
t.guru.tx9a217: PhotoThe audience. Teachers, students and families filled every row, with the aisle kept clear for the ceremony.
t.guru.txd9c2a: What designing an event taught me
t.guru.tx55b97: Being part of this initiative was a proud moment. As my first event design, it also showed me how much of UX carries over to physical spaces.
t.guru.tx00c6b: Plan the journey first. Deciding where people arrive, walk and sit made every later decision easier, just like mapping a user flow.
t.guru.tx8e42e: Hierarchy works in space too. The stage, the aisle and the reserved seating told everyone who the day was for, without a word.
t.guru.tx11688: Own the details end to end. Designing and printing every artefact myself kept the whole event consistent.
